描述_EN: de maar rarely photographs the inhabitants of these spaces but the rooms nevertheless are seen by the artist as portraits of those who live in them. marrigje de maar's series, 'home made' (2003-2006), of which this photograph is a part, is about private, domestic spaces in various countries, including the netherlands, finland, russia, china and japan. personal belongings, and the evidence of habits and daily necessities, give shape to the character of the room and the person. across cultural boundaries, desire for personal space seems to be universal. they share a sensibility with historic dutch 'golden age' paintings of domestic interiors, but combine this with distinctly modern subjects and concerns. her images are made predominantly with available natural light and require long exposures. by dealing with the notion of home de maar's images touch a common personal interest to which all viewers can relate. with this method, she is able to catch authentic states of domestic interiors and not one that is a censured or a version presented for visitors. in most cases, de maar gains admittance by going unannounced from door to door and showing a letter of introduction in the appropriate language. the photographs not only open the door to the private lives of others but also offer a possibility for reflecting on our own.
描述_ZN: de maar很少拍摄这些空间的居民，但这些房间还是被艺术家视为居住在其中的人的肖像。 Marrigje de maar的 "家庭制造 "系列（2003-2006），这张照片是其中的一部分，是关于不同国家的私人和家庭空间，包括荷兰、芬兰、俄罗斯、中国和日本。 个人物品，以及习惯和日常必需品的证据，给房间和人的性格以形状。 跨越文化的界限，对个人空间的渴望似乎是普遍的。 他们与历史上荷兰 "黄金时代 "的家庭内部绘画有着共同的感觉，但与明显的现代主题和关注相结合。 她的图像主要是用现有的自然光拍摄的，需要长时间曝光。 通过处理家的概念，de maar的图像触及了一个所有观众都能感受到的共同的个人兴趣。 通过这种方法，她能够捕捉到家庭内部的真实状态，而不是一个被指责的或为游客呈现的版本。 在大多数情况下，de maar通过挨家挨户的突击检查并出示相应语言的介绍信来获得入场券。 这些照片不仅打开了通往他人私人生活的大门，也为反思我们自己的生活提供了可能。
